system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
Jay has to draw a shape.
- It must have 5 sides.
- It must have one line of symmetry.
Jay has started to draw the shape.
Complete Jay’s shape.

[Image: an incomplete shape with three sides forming a rectangle on a grid.]

Figure, described in words:
A 10 by 10 square grid. A three-sided incomplete shape is drawn with thick black lines along the grid lines: a horizontal bottom segment 6 units long (leaving 2 units of margin on the left and 2 units on the right along the bottom edge of the grid), and two vertical segments each 4 units tall rising upward from the two ends of the bottom segment (leaving 6 units of grid space above them). The top of the shape is open.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Draw a horizontal line across the top of the two vertical sides, joining the tops of the two vertical segments, to make a rectangle. Then add a fifth side as a triangle sitting on top of the rectangle: draw two straight lines from the top-left corner and top-right corner of the rectangle up to a single point centered directly above the middle of the rectangle (on the vertical line of symmetry through the middle of the bottom segment), so the shape is a pentagon (house shape) with 5 sides: bottom, left, right, and two roof sides meeting at the apex. The one line of symmetry is the vertical line through the middle of the shape, running from the apex straight down to the middle of the bottom side.
